findings.description: storage_encrypted = false leaves the MySQL instance's storage, snapshots and automated backups unencrypted at rest.
publicly_accessible = true gives the RDS instance an internet-routable endpoint, exposing MySQL to untrusted networks and credential attacks; the only control left is the security group.

The master password comes from var.password (not marked sensitive here) and is written verbatim into Terraform state and interpolated into EC2 user data, rather than being managed by Secrets Manager (manage_master_user_password). The default 'admin' master username also aids guessing.

user_data embeds the RDS master username and password into /var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc. User data is readable in cleartext from the instance metadata service by any local process or via SSRF, leaking database master credentials.

No metadata_options block with http_tokens = "required", so IMDSv1 remains available; an SSRF in the PHP application could retrieve the user-data secrets and the instance profile credentials for the wildcard IAM role.
No root_block_device { encrypted = true } is specified, so the volume that stores the database credential file relies on AMI/account defaults and may be unencrypted at rest.

The inline policy grants s3:*, ec2:* and rds:* on Resource "*" to the role assumed by the internet-facing web server, enabling full account-wide data access, resource manipulation and privilege escalation (e.g. ec2:RunInstances with iam:PassRole-adjacent paths, rds snapshot exfiltration) if the app is compromised.
Egress allows all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0 from the database security group, removing an exfiltration/command-and-control control for a compromised, publicly reachable database host.

The MySQL 8.0 parameter group does not set require_secure_transport = 1, and the generated PHP client uses mysqli_connect with no TLS options, so credentials and employee data can traverse the network in cleartext to a publicly accessible endpoint.
Port 3306 is opened to the entire VPC CIDR instead of being restricted to the application instance's security group, so any workload in the VPC can reach the database.

findings.issue_category: web server exposed via shared security group
findings.description: The application instance is attached to aws_security_group.portal_sg and its public DNS is exported, but no HTTPS is configured - the PHP app serves plaintext HTTP over port 80 including form-submitted personal data (names/addresses), transmitting it in cleartext.
